evidence: Hays — Hays County Ranch and local grassland documentation explicitly lists Indiangrass.
Travis — Balcones Canyonlands Preserve plant list explicitly lists Sorghastrum nutans.
Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center provides a detailed Williamson County treatment.

morphology.look_here_first: Start at the collar and then the seedhead. Indiangrass is a tall warm-season perennial with a conspicuous stiff membranous ligule and auricle-like collar extensions, plus a dense golden-bronze panicle with once-bent twisted awns.
diagnostic_traits: tall perennial bunchgrass from short scaly rhizomes
stiff conspicuous membranous ligule with auricle-like extensions
single once-bent twisted awn about 10–22 mm

confusers.separator: S. elliottii is a more eastern, slender woodland/sandy-soil species; S. nutans is the familiar robust tallgrass-prairie Indiangrass with a dense golden panicle and strong collar/ligule cue.
